notes: The broken-environment-variable ground truth first said ResourceNotFoundException. The logs showed AccessDeniedException: ShopLite's role only covers its own table, so IAM refuses the call before DynamoDB looks for the table. NightWatch's diagnosis was right and the ground truth was corrected after the run. The score is unchanged, because the hypothesis names TABLE_NAME.

CI redeployed ShopLite as version 12 (a change to the canary) just before the run, so that deploy appears in the first scenario's change history. The error-flag diagnosis mentions version 12 next to the flag change.

A first attempt the same day was stopped after 2 scenarios. It blamed the bad deploy on the previous scenario's flag change, because a 30-minute log window still held that scenario's errors, and the lab counted one incident twice. Both were fixed (ADR 0013) and all 7 scenarios were run again. The first attempt's partial results are not included.

bad-deploy.ground_truth: Commit 'read product prices from the new price field' was deployed and makes product listings and orders raise KeyError: 'price'.
bad-deploy.name: bad deploy
bad-deploy.top_hypothesis: Version 13 of shoplite‑api (sha=28af2eda514c) introduced a KeyError on missing 'price' field, leading to 30 errors and 5xx rate >5%

broken-env-var.ground_truth: A new version changed only the TABLE_NAME environment variable, to a table that doesn't exist and that ShopLite's role isn't allowed to use, so every DynamoDB call fails with AccessDeniedException (IAM refuses the call before DynamoDB looks for the table).
broken-env-var.name: broken environment variable
broken-env-var.top_hypothesis: Deploy of version 14 changed TABLE_NAME to shoplite-catalogue, but the Lambda’s execution role lacks dynamodb:Query permission on that table, leading to AccessDeniedException errors and the observed 5xx rate and Lambda error alarms.

dependency-latency.ground_truth: The extra_latency_ms flag adds 1.5 s to every request, like a slow dependency, so p95 latency stays above the 1-second alarm.
dependency-latency.name: slow dependency
dependency-latency.top_hypothesis: Setting /shoplite/flags to {"extra_latency_ms":1500} introduced artificial delay in the Lambda, causing p95 latency to exceed 1000 ms.

dynamodb-throttle.ground_truth: The shoplite table's read capacity was lowered from 5 units to 1, so product reads are throttled (ProvisionedThroughputExceededException).
dynamodb-throttle.name: DynamoDB throttling
dynamodb-throttle.top_hypothesis: Capacity reduction of the shoplite DynamoDB table (read capacity set to 1 unit) caused read throttling, which manifested as ProvisionedThroughputExceededException errors in the shoplite‑api Lambda (version 12, sha efc0fd6d7f19) and spiked Lambda error count, triggering both alarms.

error-flag.ground_truth: ShopLite's error flag (/shoplite/flags) was switched on, so requests fail with InjectedFaultError.
error-flag.name: error flag (error_rate=0.8)
error-flag.top_hypothesis: A recent SSM parameter change set /shoplite/flags error_rate to 0.8, and the new Lambda code (version 12) respects this flag and deliberately injects faults, leading to >=2 errors per minute and triggering the alarm.

lambda-timeout.ground_truth: The hang flag in /shoplite/flags makes every request run past ShopLite's 5-second timeout, so Lambda stops it ('Task timed out').
lambda-timeout.name: Lambda timeout
lambda-timeout.top_hypothesis: The recent SSM flag change to {"hang": true} (E5) caused the live Lambda version 12 (sha=efc0fd6d7f19, E14) to hang, leading to timeouts, high p95 latency (E13) and increased error count (E11), which directly triggered the three alarms (E2‑E4).

memory-exhaustion.ground_truth: The memory_hog_mb flag makes every request allocate 400 MB, more than the function's 256 MB, so the runtime runs out of memory and is killed.
memory-exhaustion.name: memory exhaustion
memory-exhaustion.top_hypothesis: The recent SSM flag change adding 400 MB of artificial memory usage caused the Lambda (version 12) to run out of memory, producing Runtime.OutOfMemory errors and elevated latency, which triggered the shoplite-5xx-rate alarm.
